interface.longDescription:
Manage customer support for website live chat, WhatsApp, Instagram DMs, Facebook Messenger, and email in one shared inbox. Connect Chatway to ChatGPT to review customer messages, find conversation history, and draft or send replies.

Chatway gives your team a customizable live chat widget, a shared inbox, and a help center. Use AI to answer common questions, route conversations to the right teammates, and support customers from the web, iOS, or Android.

In ChatGPT, start with your unresolved conversations to see what needs attention. Look up a customer by name or email, summarize their support history, and search your knowledge base before drafting a reply. Ask ChatGPT to send it when you’re ready. For automatic replies to incoming messages, set up a separate automation or connect an always-on AI agent.

You can also add private notes and tags, assign conversations to teammates, and resolve or reopen conversations. If a Chatway AI assistant is handling a conversation that needs a teammate, request a human handoff.

The plugin works within the permissions you grant when connecting your workspace. Chatway also offers MCP, an API, and webhooks for teams building their own support workflows.

Install the plugin and create a Chatway account during setup, or sign in to your existing account.
capabilities: Review and reply to Instagram DMs
Respond to website live chat messages
Review and reply to customer support emails
Review customer messages in an omnichannel shared inbox
Draft AI-assisted replies using your knowledge base
Track customer service follow-ups with private notes and tags
Hand off AI-handled conversations to human support
defaultPrompt: What needs a reply first across WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, website live chat, and email?
Draft replies to my latest support tickets using my knowledge base. Send only the replies I approve.
What were the top 3 recurring issues in last week's support conversations? Show examples and suggest an FAQ for each.

positive.description: Triage a populated reviewer inbox. Setup: the reviewer workspace contains at least five accessible unresolved conversations with distinct contacts and messages.
positive.prompt: Show me my 5 most recent unresolved Chatway conversations, including each contact name, last message preview, and whether it is resolved.
positive.expected_behavior: Call list-conversations once with status=unresolved, page=1, and per_page=5. Return no more than five conversations in newest-first order. For every result, use only the returned contact, last_message, and is_resolved fields; all displayed conversations must be unresolved.

positive.description: Find one known customer conversation. Setup: the reviewer workspace contains exactly one accessible conversation for contact reviewer.search@example.com.
positive.prompt: Find the Chatway conversation for reviewer.search@example.com and summarize its contact and current resolution status.
positive.expected_behavior: Call search-conversations with query=reviewer.search@example.com. Use the single returned conversation ID with get-conversation. Report the returned contact and resolution status without reading message history or inventing details.

positive.description: Draft a knowledge-grounded reply for a known fixture. Setup: reviewer.product@example.com has exactly one accessible conversation asking about returns, and the workspace knowledge base contains a Q&A matching the query return policy.
positive.prompt: Read the Chatway conversation for reviewer.product@example.com, search the knowledge base for return policy, and draft a reply without sending it.
positive.expected_behavior: Search for reviewer.product@example.com, retrieve the returned conversation and its messages, and search the knowledge base with query=return policy. Draft a reply supported only by the returned messages and knowledge-base content. Do not call send-message or claim the draft was sent.

positive.description: Add an internal note to a dedicated fixture. Setup: reviewer.note@example.com has exactly one accessible conversation reserved for this test.
positive.prompt: Find the Chatway conversation for reviewer.note@example.com and add the private note: Reviewed by support; follow up tomorrow.
positive.expected_behavior: Search for reviewer.note@example.com, use the single returned conversation ID, and call add-note with the exact content Reviewed by support; follow up tomorrow. Report the returned confirmation and identify the note as internal; do not send a customer-visible message.

positive.description: Request handoff on a dedicated fixture. Setup: reviewer.handoff@example.com has exactly one accessible unresolved conversation that is currently handled by a Chatway AI assistant and has no existing handoff request.
positive.prompt: Find the Chatway conversation for reviewer.handoff@example.com and request a human handoff.
positive.expected_behavior: Search for reviewer.handoff@example.com, use the single returned conversation ID, call handoff-to-human, and report the returned handoff_requested status. Do not claim that a human has joined or replied.

negative.description: Unsupported outbound channel action. No Chatway tool should be called because this integration cannot send SMS; explain the limitation without claiming delivery.
negative.prompt: Send an SMS to this customer using Chatway.

negative.description: Unsupported billing administration. No Chatway tool should be called because the integration cannot create plans or change subscriptions; explain that billing administration is unavailable.
negative.prompt: Create a new Chatway billing plan and change the workspace subscription.

negative.description: Unsupported external CRM operation. No Chatway tool should be called because the integration cannot create Salesforce records or assign Salesforce users; explain the limitation.
negative.prompt: Create a Salesforce opportunity from this Chatway conversation and assign it to a Salesforce user.
